answer: A restaurant renovation checklist works in three stages. Before the lease, confirm zoning and the unit's occupancy permit. Before construction, get floor plans through public health review and get your City permits. Before opening, finish inspections, get any occupancy permit and give the inspector at least five working days' notice.

Every week of delay is lost revenue, so a restaurant renovation checklist is worth working through early, and choosing the right restaurant renovation company matters as much as the design.

blocks.x: Restaurant renovation checklist by stage

A restaurant in Winnipeg typically needs approvals from the City, a public health inspector and, if you serve alcohol, the Liquor, Gaming and Cannabis Authority of Manitoba (LGCA). Permit and approval timelines often decide your opening date, so start them early. Our guide to [restaurant renovation permits in Winnipeg](/blog/restaurant-renovation-permits-winnipeg) covers each one in detail.
Before you sign the lease

**Zoning:** confirm with the City that a restaurant is allowed on the site before you pay for plans. A change in zoning use goes through a [development permit application](https://legacy.winnipeg.ca/ppd/Documents/Permits/Commercial/Change-in-Occupancy-Requirements.pdf).

**Occupancy:** check what the unit's occupancy permit covers. Turning a store or office into a restaurant is a change of use. It starts with a building permit application, then an [occupancy permit](/blog/occupancy-permit-change-of-use-winnipeg).

**Drawings:** ask whether you need an architect or engineer. Sealed drawings are called for when a Part 3 building has a [change in major occupancy classification](https://www.winnipeg.ca/media/6330).

**Walk-through:** have a contractor walk the space with you, looking at exhaust routes, drains, power and gas. In an older building, have suspect materials [tested for asbestos](/blog/asbestos-testing-before-renovating-manitoba) before anything is torn out.
Before construction starts

**Public health approval:** submit the registration form, your menu and scaled floor plans with equipment listed to your [public health inspector](https://gov.mb.ca/health/publichealth/environmentalhealth/protection/food.html) before any construction or renovation, and get a permit before opening. If plans change later, contact the inspector first with a revised plan.

**Filing inside Winnipeg:** the [provincial guideline](https://www.gov.mb.ca/health/publichealth/environmentalhealth/protection/docs/construction.pdf) says plans and specifications go to the City's One Stop Plan Approval office at Unit 31-30 Fort Street, so ask your inspector how to file.
**City permits:** a City of Winnipeg building permit for the renovation, plus the plumbing, mechanical and electrical permits your work needs, which City-licensed contractors apply for.

**Hood and fire suppression:** settle the menu first. [Manitoba's guideline](https://www.gov.mb.ca/health/publichealth/environmentalhealth/protection/docs/construction.pdf) requires an approved Type I or Type II hood suited to the menu, so consult the permit authority and your inspector on the hood and fire suppression system.
**Grease interceptor:** settle its size and location at the plan stage, since it's hard to move later.

**Liquor licensing:** a liquor service licence from the Liquor, Gaming and Cannabis Authority of Manitoba if you'll serve alcohol. If you already hold one, [it's your responsibility to tell the LGCA](https://lgcamb.ca/liquor/liquor-service-licences-2/how-to-apply/) about major renovations.
**Timing:** mark your slowest weeks for heavy work. Our guide covers [when to renovate a restaurant or bar](/blog/hospitality-renovation-winnipeg-off-season).
**Long-lead items:** ask suppliers how long hoods and equipment will take, and order early.
Before you open

**Inspections and occupancy:** finish the City's inspections and, where one is required, get a [final or interim occupancy permit](https://www.winnipeg.ca/media/6131). Stocking shelves, training staff and conducting business wait until it is issued.
**Hood sign-off:** get written confirmation from the authority having jurisdiction that the ventilation system meets fire and building codes. The health permit waits for it.
**Opening inspection:** give your public health inspector at least five working days' notice. The health permit is issued only after the inspection, once construction is complete.
**Liquor licence:** the LGCA lists zoning, occupancy and fire safety, and health approvals among its requirements, so allow for them in your timeline.
This is general information, not legal advice. Requirements depend on your space and scope, and outside Winnipeg your local permit authority takes the City's role.
Converting a non-restaurant space

Taking over a former retail or office unit usually takes more work than taking over a former restaurant. Expect new exhaust, a grease interceptor, upgraded plumbing and electrical, and code upgrades for the new use. A contractor walk-through **before** you sign the lease can save you from a space that's too expensive to convert.
Restaurant renovation checklist: questions to ask a contractor
Can you give us references from recent, similar work?
Do you coordinate the hood, fire suppression and kitchen equipment suppliers?
Who handles permits and inspections, including public health?
What's the realistic schedule from permit to opening?
How do you handle long-lead items like hoods and equipment?
Can you work after hours if we're renovating an operating restaurant?
For the public-record checks worth doing on any contractor, see our guide on [how to choose a renovation contractor](/blog/how-to-choose-the-right-contractor-for-your-renovation-project).
Keeping an existing restaurant open
Phase dining room work around service hours
Schedule kitchen work for planned closures, ideally in slower months
Plan loud work around the [City's noise hours](https://www.winnipeg.ca/building-development/property-records/construction-your-neighbourhood): within 150 metres of a home, it must stop at 9 p.m.
Keep washrooms and exits available
Protect food areas from dust
The bottom line
Work through the stages in order, and choose a restaurant renovation company that can explain how it will handle your kitchen, your permits and your first inspection.
